the phase fluctuations of Cooper-pairs are strongly enhanced in the underdopedsuperconducting regime of high-Tc cuprates, and that this is a direct consequence of a strong spin-fluctuation pairing interaction.
the underdoped region of the phase diagram is dominated by phase fluctuations and that this is in agreement with experiments.
the superfluid density and the superconducting phase coherence temperature are reduced by phase fluctuations, and the pseudogap temperature is increased by the spin fluctuation pairing.

a theoretical study of the electronic properties of cuprate superconductivity.
the theoretical analysis of Cooper-pairs in underdoped superconductors.
the theoretical description of the superconducting phase transition and the superconducting state in the high temperature superconductors.

the underdoped superconductors are in the crossover from the BCS to the BEC limit.

phase fluctuations are a key ingredient to understand the underdoped superconducting cuprates and that the pseudogap temperature is a measure for the onset of the phase fluctuations.
